title: Fix ambiguous-delimiter token attribution for interrupted streaming sessions
creator: Ava Chen
description: Streaming requests that contain ambiguous delimiter sequences (for example, '\n--BOUNDARY--\n' fragments or repeated whitespace+punctuation) are occasionally split across stream fragments such that the tokenizer state used for final token accounting diverges from the state used by the model runtime. When a mid-stream fallback or abort occurs, our metering pipeline sometimes credits output tokens to the wrong side (input vs. output) or double-counts tokens across fragments. The issue affects long-lived streaming sessions and clients using chunked uploads or unreliable networks.
steps_to_reproduce: Open a streaming generation session with a long prompt that contains deliberate delimiter-like sequences (e.g., repeated '\n---\n' or '##END##' markers) and set client-side chunking to small sizes (~128-512 bytes).
Force an in-flight model switch (fallback to smaller model) or abort the stream halfway through a delimiter sequence using test harness (see test case harness: /internal/test-harness/stream-abort).

Observe token counts in the metering audit log and compare the per-fragment tokenizer checkpoints to the runtime KV cache offsets. You should see mismatches where input bytes are attributed as generated tokens or where the same logical token appears in two fragments and is double-credited.
Reproduce with both UTF-8 multibyte characters and ASCII-only payloads — problem appears in both but is sensitive to chunk boundaries near multibyte codepoints.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-02): found mismatch between tokenizer checkpoint stored in stream metadata and the tokenizer state used by compiled runtime during fallback path. Root cause appears to be that the metering service reconstructs tokenization using a separate incremental tokenizer implementation that assumes fragment boundaries are always token-aligned.
Sentry traces show ~0.8% of streaming sessions in the last 30d had checksum mismatches between metering and runtime token counts; higher in regions with high-LAN jitter (eu-west-2 test cluster).

Observed three concrete failure modes: (1) delimiter split across fragments, tokenizer reconsiders boundary and creates extra token; (2) fallback mid-fragment where runtime had consumed prefix but metering replay does not see consumed KV cache, leading to attributing some output tokens to input; (3) multi-byte char split causing tokenizer to produce a replacement token on replay, shifting counts.
Telemetry: added temporary debug flag showing tokenizer state hashes on stream open/close. Hash divergence correlated strongly with sessions that had network re-ordering or retries.
proposed_fix: Unify tokenizer state by shipping a compact tokenizer checkpoint (tokenizer id + byte offset + state-hash + last-whitespace-flag) from the runtime at every fragment boundary to the metering pipeline. On fallback/abort, use runtime-supplied checkpoints to reconcile token counts. Additionally, treat ambiguous delimiter sequences as 'sticky' boundaries: if a delimiter tokenization crosses a fragment boundary, mark the fragment as non-final for replay until the delimiter completes or a deterministic boundary is observed.
implementation_plan: Add lightweight tokenizer checkpoint struct to stream protocol (protocol buffer change) — minimal fields to keep backward compatibility.
Update runtime to emit checkpoints at configurable intervals (default: every 1KB or every '\n' boundary, whichever comes first).
Modify metering pipeline to prefer runtime checkpoints over speculative replay when available; if no checkpoint present, continue best-effort replay but mark event for later manual audit.

Add migration: allow older clients to continue without checkpoints and run a periodic reconciliation job that uses S3 stored fragments plus runtime logs to retroactively fix billing anomalies for impacted sessions in the last 90 days.
Prepare a feature flag to enable the new checkpointing in canary clusters and run for 2 weeks before global rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Metering audit shows <0.01% checksum mismatches between runtime and metering for canary cluster traffic for two consecutive weeks.
No customer-reported billing spikes related to streaming delimiter edge cases after rollout for the canary cohort (tracked via billing-alerting dashboard).
Migration job successfully reconciles known historical mismatches for at least 95% of affected sessions within a 3-day window, with manual tickets created for the remainder.
Unit and integration tests cover multi-byte codepoint splits, delimiter-cross-boundary cases, and mid-fragment fallback scenarios.
testing_plan: Create synthetic load tests that vary chunk sizes, presence of delimiter-like sequences, and injection of mid-stream aborts. Use both BPE and byte-level tokenizers in test matrix.
Run canary with 5% production traffic from eu-west-2 to exercise real network jitter; monitor checksum metric and SLOs for added telemetry overhead.
Add regression test to CI that replays previously failing Sentry session traces and asserts stable token accounting after patch.
Perform end-to-end billing e2e test that ensures invoices/usage records reflect reconciled counts and that quota consumption aligns with runtime numbers.
